title: User manuals for machinery and equipment
description: The main objectives of creating a user manual from AIoT P.S.A.’s perspective:

blocks.text: The main objectives of creating a user manual from AIoT P.S.A.’s perspective:

items: – Safety: Providing information on safe usage rules to prevent accidents.
– Legal requirements: Providing the required technical documentation, particularly when launching products onto the market.
– Minimising breakdowns: Maintenance tips extend the service life of the equipment. Reducing operating costs: Technical support becomes less necessary when the user can find answers in the manual.
– Correct operation: Guiding the user step by step to facilitate installation and operation.

blocks.text: The entire life cycle of the machine in one manual
The manual should guide the user through the entire life cycle of the machine:

items: Title page: Machine name, model, type, CE marking, manufacturer’s details.
Safety (Health and Safety) – key section: Warnings, pictograms, description of residual risks, required personal protective equipment.
Technical description: Construction, main components, operating principle, technical parameters (drawings, diagrams).
Installation and commissioning: Assembly, connection to utilities (electricity, air), initial start-up. Operation: Start-up/shutdown procedures, normal operation, and abnormal situations.
Maintenance and repairs: Routine tasks, adjustments, and a list of spare parts. Troubleshooting: Fault table and methods of rectification.

blocks.text: We avoid technical jargon wherever possible. We write briefly, concisely and unambiguously.
We use photos, technical drawings and diagrams instead of long descriptions.
We clearly highlight risks to life or health (e.g. a box, red colour, the word "DANGER").
Different language for a maintenance technician, different for an operator.
We guarantee compliance of the documentation with the latest regulations:
The instructions must be available in the language of the country where the machine is used (in Poland – in Polish).
Compliance with the new Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 (from 2027) or the Machinery Directive 2006/42/EC.
The instructions must include information on ‘foreseeable misuse’.
Understanding the machine, discussions with its designers and operators.
Gathering drawings, diagrams and technical documentation
Creating content (ideally whilst testing the machine – this helps to spot errors in the description).
